subject: Dealing with variable dimensions in 1 model file

messages.author: 26a87d764f5562dc
messages.subject: Dealing with variable dimensions in 1 model file
parts:
Hello,

I have a sampler where the dimensions of the data may vary from a vector to an array. I'm wondering if there is a way to make nimble happy specifying it as an array with some dimensions being 1 sometimes.

Say you observe n.cov covariates on M individuals with n.rep replications and I have a function like this:

object <-function(data[1:M,1:n.cov,1:n.rep])

If n.cov and n.rep > 1, nimble is happy with this array. But if either n.cov or n.rep =1, nimble is not. Is there a way to make nimble happy with arrays where one or more dimensions are of size 1? Otherwise, I need 3 model files and determining which to use is confusing for other users. It would be great if I could use just 1 model file.

Thanks!

Ben Augustine

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Dealing with variable dimensions in 1 model file
parts:
Hi Ben,

Good to hear from you.  Unfortunately this is still a bumpy part of the system. 

A few options:

You could make variants of 'function' and determine which is included in a model using definition-time if-then-else. (This allows if-then-else in model code that is resolved permanently during nimbleModel).

You could make a scheme like this: function(data[1:M, 1:(n.cov+1), 1:n.rep], n.cov = n.cov) where you have padded 'data' where needed and then via a separate argument give 'function' the information it needs on whether padding is involved (e.g. the actual value of n.cov).

You could re-arrange data with the first dimension being of size M*n.cov and then take care of indexing correctly within that inside of 'function'.

We know it's a hassle and it's on our minds.

-Perry

Thanks Perry!

The first option is interesting, I'll have to look into it more. Though, I also have custom updates and the dimensionality in those would need to match the model file, so I don't think that will work fully in this case unless if what you propose could also select the correct custom update functions.

I've used the padding option before. I should probably just commit to doing that.

Thanks again for all the help!

Ben
